modal-dialog.modal-heading: What counts as a foreign financial account?

ul.li: Bank accounts such as savings and checking accounts, and time deposits
Securities accounts, such as brokerage accounts, securities derivatives accounts, or other financial instruments accounts
Commodity futures or options accounts
Insurance or annuity policies with a cash value (such as a whole life insurance policy)
Mutual funds or similar pooled funds
Any other accounts maintained in a foreign financial institution or with a person performing the services of a financial institution

p.strong: How do I know if an account is considered foreign?

modal-content.p: Where the account itself is physically located determines if it is considered a foreign financial account. The account location, not the nationality of the financial institution, is what counts for this question.

ul.li: A savings account at a U.S. bank that is maintained with a branch physically located in France is an example of a foreign account
A savings account at a French bank that is maintained with a branch physically located in the U.S. is not foreign

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What is a financial interest or signature authority?

modal-content.p: You have a financial interest in a financial account if

ul.li: you’re the owner of record or holder of legal title (even if the account is maintained for someone else’s benefit)
the owner of record or holder of legal title is your agent or representative or someone else acting on your behalf with respect to the account
the owner of record or holder of legal title is an entity (including a corporation, partnership, or trust) in which you have certain direct or indirect interest

p.a: Learn more about financial interest in foreign financial accounts.

modal-content.p: You have "signature authority" over a financial account if you (alone or together with someone else) have authority to control the disposition of the assets in the account by direct communication with the financial institution maintaining the account.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What counts as a foreign trust?

modal-content.p: A trust is a legal document in which someone dictates how their assets get transferred to others. People who create a trust, also known as "grantors," authorize certain individuals or institutions to hold, manage, and distribute assets they put in trust for beneficiaries, like charities or family members. Assets can include things like money, property, accounts, and more.

p.strong: How do I know if a trust is considered foreign?

modal-content.p: Unless both of the following are true of a trust, it’s considered foreign:

ol.li: a court in the United States exercises primary supervision over the trust; and
one or more United States persons have authority to control all substantial decisions of the trust (and no other person has veto power).

p.a: Learn more about foreign trust reporting requirements

div.h2: Direct File doesn’t yet support the forms required to report digital assets.

heading.a: Find other ways to file your federal taxes.

modal-content.p: The most common and well known digital assets are cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, and non-fungible tokens (NFTs). Digital assets also include other less common assets that are digital representations of value that are recorded on a cryptographically secured distributed ledger or similar technology.

Online payments with U.S. dollars are not digital asset transactions. The U.S. dollar is not a digital asset even when sent or received from your phone or computer. For example, using an online peer-to-peer payment app or service such as Venmo, PayPal, or Zelle to send or receive U.S. dollars is not considered a digital asset.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What does it mean to receive a digital asset?

modal-content.p: You received a digital asset if you:

ul.li: Exchanged digital assets as payment for goods or services or in exchange for property or services including other digital assets
Got digital assets as a reward or award
Got digital assets from mining, staking, and similar activities
Got digital assets as a result of a "hard fork"

modal-content.p: Some things won’t count as receiving digital assets, such as if you:

ul.li: Bought digital assets with U.S. dollars or a foreign currency
Held digital assets in your own wallets or accounts
Transferred digital assets between your own wallets or accounts

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What counts as selling, exchanging, or disposing of a digital asset?

modal-content.p: You sold, exchanged, or disposed of a digital asset if you:

ul.li: Paid for goods or services with digital assets
Exchanged digital assets for property including other digital assets
Sold a digital asset for cash
Otherwise sold, exchanged, or disposed of any financial interest in a digital asset

modal-dialog.modal-heading: How do I know if I made a contribution to an Individual Retirement Arrangement (IRA)?

modal-content.p: IRAs are tax-advantaged savings plans for retirement. Common types of IRAs include Traditional IRAs, Roth IRAs, SEP IRA plans, and SIMPLE IRA plans.
If you have an IRA, check with the financial institution to learn if you made contributions for .

The institution may have also sent you a Form 5498, which documents your IRA contributions. However, these forms may not arrive until May, since contributions are allowed until the tax filing deadline (usually April 15).
